title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching, add quant profiles, unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce autotune defaults for batching and caching, add model quantization profile presets, and expose unit-economics tooling in the console. Backwards compatible; rollout behind feature flag.
description: Context: Hosting customers are running a wide range of workloads with varying sequence length distributions. Engineering thesis: sensible defaults for batching/caching plus model quantization profiles reduce per-token cost for 70% of workloads without developer changes. This PR implements: 1) autotune default settings for request batching and KV-prefix caching at the router/runtime level, 2) a small set of verified quantization profiles and a selection mechanism tied to model family + latency SLO, 3) a lightweight unit-economics tool and API that exposes estimated cost-per-token and expected throughput under current settings. The description below is a single continuous block but contains the checklist and testing notes. Changes in this PR: - Add autotune module that suggests default batch/window sizes based on recent request histograms and model latency curves - Persist suggested defaults per-tenant in config store and surface in Console with opt-out - Add quantization profiles (fp16, int8-q4_0, int8-q4_1) metadata and runtime selection heuristics - Integrate quant profiles with warm-start cache to avoid cold-start regressions - Add unit-econ CLI subcommand and new /internal/uecon API endpoint to estimate cost/throughput for a given deployment profile - Add feature flag `uecon.autotune_defaults` to gate rollout Checklist: - [x] Design review: ENG-6123, ENG-6155 - [x] Perf bench: microbenchmarks for 4 model families (small/medium/large) - [x] E2E tests for autotune decision loop - [x] Console UX reviewed by product - [x] Security review for config persistence (no secrets stored) - [x] Feature-flagged rollout plan Testing / How to validate: - Unit tests cover heuristic math and selection logic (run `pytest -k autotune`) - Integration test: deploy to perf-canary cluster and run `uecon estimate` against synthetic traces in tools/perf - Manual verification: enable feature flag for a single tenant, run workload generator, confirm token unit cost decreases or remains stable while latency SLOs hold - Can monitor via new dashboard panels: "UEcon: estimated cost/token" and "Autotune decisions" Rollout plan: - Canary (1 tenant) -> Regional canaries (3 customers) -> Gradual ramp (50%, 100%) - Keep feature flag on by default only after 2 weeks of stable metrics Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the autotune loop conservative: suggestions require 3 windows of stable observations and will not override explicit customer config. The quant profiles include a fallback to fp16 for models that show >2x latency regression. See related Linear items ENG-6123 and ENG-6155 for design doc and benchmarks.

review_comments: Ravi Patel: Nice work. Can we make the 3-window requirement configurable per-tenant? Suggestion: add a tenant_override TTL to avoid oscillation.
Maya Chen: Good call. Added tenant_override and a TTL config (defaults to 24h). See config/tenant_autotune.yaml in next commit.
Lucia Alvarez: Benchmarks look promising, but we need a regression test to ensure no P95 latency spike on long-context models.
Maya Chen: Added bench_autotune.py and an e2e perf test that runs on canary. Also added fallback to fp16 when latency >2x baseline.
Samir Khan: CI flake on integration test container  reran and passed. Approving pending small nits in doc strings.
ci_checks: perf-smoke: pass (microbenchmarks show ~18-34% cost improvement on tested workloads)
notes_on_risks: Conservative defaults and feature-flag limit blast radius. Primary risk is transient latency regression for long-context workloads; mitigated by fp16 fallback and circuit-breaker thresholds.
testing_instructions: Run pytest -k autotune; run cli: python -m cli.uecon estimate --profile perf-canary; enable feature flag uecon.autotune_defaults for canary tenant and monitor UEcon dashboard panels.
user_impact: No breaking changes. Customers who rely on explicit batching/caching settings are unaffected unless they enable the autotune feature. Default is off for existing tenants until rollout.
